c_botulinum_nonproteolytic.name: Clostridium botulinum (Non-Proteolytic Types B, E, F)
c_botulinum_nonproteolytic.toxinProduction: Produces lethal botulinum neurotoxin in anaerobic environments (vacuum pouches). Can germinate and produce neurotoxin at refrigeration temperatures as low as 38°F (3.3°C).
c_botulinum_nonproteolytic.criticalSafetyRule: Food held in anaerobic vacuum sealed pouches between 40°F and 126°F for more than 2 hours poses high botulism neurotoxin risk. Sous vide bath must maintain >= 130°F (54.4°C) for extended cooks (> 2 hours). If cooking below 130°F (e.g. rare salmon at 115°F), total time from fridge to plate must not exceed 2 hours.

c_perfringens.name: Clostridium perfringens
c_perfringens.dangerNote: Fastest multiplying bacterial pathogen in food; doubling time 7 to 10 minutes at 109°F-117°F (43°C-47°C). Rapidly multiplies if warm-up to 130°F takes > 2 hours or if cooling cooked pouches to < 41°F takes > 6 hours.

pouchMaterials.name: Platinum-Cured Food-Grade Silicone (e.g. Stasher)
pouchMaterials.description: Cross-linked with pure platinum catalyst, devoid of peroxides, phthalates, BPA/BPS, and heavy metals. Withstands boiling water and extended 72-hour cooks with zero chemical leaching into lipids.

pouchMaterials.name: Co-Extruded Multi-Layer PE / PA Nylon Vacuum Pouches
pouchMaterials.lipidExtractionResistance: Good (PA outer barrier stops gas, PE inner seal)
pouchMaterials.safetyRating: Certified Safe for Commercial Sous Vide
pouchMaterials.description: Standard commercial vacuum packaging (FoodSaver, VacMaster). Inner layer is pure virgin food-grade polyethylene; outer layer is high-barrier polyamide nylon. Excellent oxygen barrier preventing spoilage.

pouchMaterials.name: Polypropylene (PP) Retort Pouches
pouchMaterials.description: Medical and commercial retort grade material engineered to endure autoclave steam sterilization at 250°F. Outstanding resistance to hot fat extraction.

pouchMaterials.name: Heavy-Duty LDPE Freezer Bags (e.g. Ziploc Freezer)
pouchMaterials.description: Polyethylene softens near 158°F and melts at 195°F. Suitable only for low-temperature cooking (130°F-150°F). Avoid fatty meats over 12 hours as polyolefin slip additives (erucamide) dissolve in lipids.

pouchMaterials.name: Thin Economy Sandwich / Snack Bags
pouchMaterials.description: Never use economy thin sandwich bags for sous vide. Seams rupture under water pressure and thin polymer film sheds microplastics rapidly into warm meat juices.

pouchMaterials.name: PVC Cling Film / Non-Rated Commercial Wrap
pouchMaterials.phthalates: High (Contains DEHP, DINP or DEHA plasticizers)
pouchMaterials.lipidExtractionResistance: Catastrophic (DEHA extracts into fat within minutes)
pouchMaterials.description: Plasticized PVC relies on lipophilic adipates (DEHA) and ortho-phthalates to remain pliable. Under warm water bath immersion with fatty meats, up to 90% of plasticizers migrate into the meat. Strictly prohibited for cooking.

foodMatrices.name: High-Fat Meat (Ribeye, Pork Belly, Duck Confit, Lamb Chops)
Long-Cook Collagen Roasts (Short Ribs, Chuck Roast, Brisket)

severeDanger.explanation: Active microbial growth zone. Non-proteolytic C. botulinum germinates and produces fatal neurotoxin. C. perfringens doubles every 8 minutes. Must not exceed 2 hours total time.

transitionZone.explanation: Pathogens slow down, but thermal lethality is too low for reliable pasteurization. Food must be consumed immediately within 2 hours. Never chill and store.

pasteurizationSafe.explanation: Pathogen multiplication ceases. Vegetative Listeria, Salmonella, and E. coli undergo exponential thermal destruction (D-value kinetics). Safe for extended multi-day cooks.

highHeatVegetable.explanation: Required to soften plant hemicellulose and pectin. Plastic pouch must be rated for high heat (Silicone, Retort PP, or heavy Nylon/PE); standard zipper bags will burst seams.
